anchor: The SMPTE/EBU broadcast color-bar test pattern and the master-control tally light — the iconic image of a television screen under calibration and measurement — read as the emblem of a corpus whose contested core is the measured screen: automatic content recognition (ACR) silently fingerprinting the living-room glass to target and score political ads.
rationale: This corpus is about the smart-TV screen turned into a measurement instrument — ACR watching the glass, voter files matched to households, 'incrementality' lift graded by the very vendors selling the inventory. The broadcast test card is the literal artifact of a screen being calibrated, and its magenta/cyan/yellow chroma bars are neither red nor blue — sidestepping partisan cliché while staying native to television engineering. Magenta is the calibration spark (the SMPTE bar with no political valence); the chroma bars become the figure ramp; condensed broadcast-chyron type and a scanline rule complete the master-control world. It diverges hard from the warm-serif and cool-teal/cobalt ad-tech siblings.
